- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > 0.17 negative values in recent days), model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent highs.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or adjust downward by 3–5% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is positive but price history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive downward moves), model overestimates continuation — reduce forecast by 2–4% per negative sentiment signal.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often underestimates volatility — increase forecast variance by 1–2% of recent 7-day range.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early-term decline (first 7–10 days) — apply downward bias of 3–5% for first 7 days if sentiment is negative.
- If sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive positive values), model often fails to capture momentum decay — reduce forecast slope by 10–15% after 5th day of positive sentiment.
